mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during tightening episodes (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 2.0% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) followed by a subsequent decline predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates an impending labor market softening and rate cut.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases then decreases in the next two months
failure_condition: No significant positive return over 60 days when the PAYEMS pattern occurs, or unemployment remains below 4% throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests weakening supply-side momentum, which is associated with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
regime_hint: early softening in supply chain activity
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when INDPRO declines by >2%, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) falls below 2% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as investors anticipate a less restrictive policy environment.
failure_condition: No positive 20-day forward return when CPIAUCSL stays below 2% for two months, or the effect reverses in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three months triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as markets price in recession risk.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive during such UNRATE episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not available in the catalog; fallback to HOUST as a demand proxy) above 1,000K units predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return through optimism about consumer demand.
failure_condition: No positive 60-day return when HOUST exceeds 1,000 for two months, or the effect is not robust across multiple cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) below 120K followed by a rebound is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as the job market recovers.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 120K then increases in the following month
failure_condition: No positive 20-day return when the PAYEMS pattern occurs, or the rebound is not followed by positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (INDPRO) below 110 for three months indicates structural softness, predicting a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced growth prospects.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative during such INDPRO declines, or the effect is not statistically significant.
